conclusion: Slot160 is user/aperture-relative device mapping address, not firmware-root alias. Native flag bit0 selects wrapping base subtraction. Caller must bind actual owning aperture and retain mapping; Linux context_base equivalence still requires selected resource aperture binding.

vtable_evidence.slot_160_baseclass_semantics: Tailcalls slot0x158; AGX subclasses optionally subtract owning aperture base

integration_route: Descriptor TA inputs use the selected mapping user address; fragment inputs use its device address. No extra global firmware-root mapping follows from these getter calls. Ordinary Linux aperture base must be bound to the actual retained VM resource mapping, rather than copied from an unrelated resource.

gravity_caller_binding.selection: Parameters::set_private selects Linux render aperture base; valid bounds retained TA resources within its four-GiB window. Map native ordinary TA user pointers by this selected base, fragment by original device address.
gravity_caller_binding.remaining_hypothesis: Linux selected render aperture is equivalent to native allocator region1 for ordinary jobs; actual GPU execution remains unproved.
